# Populated schema-7 migration fixture

This is original synthetic GramLab data, generated offline with the untouched Python package
exported from assignment base `c901ce2010a1fa79d3fd8b0f9f5ebb68df728a82`. The imported
`src/gramlab/world.py` SHA-256 was
`39a1174c612e7fc928e90bb675bc0562ac88ac9732f1c0652c46e79f7325ff38`.
Generation happened before the schema-8 implementation. No schema-8 database was downgraded.

`world.sql` is SQLite's dump of that actual populated database, followed by its observed
`user_version=7` (SQLite's dump omits that pragma). Tests restore the original WAL journal mode.
`expected.json` contains literal complete public observations from that implementation; downloads
are stored as exact hexadecimal bytes. `identities.json` records the actual randomly allocated
local capabilities and file IDs needed to repeat those calls. All capabilities are synthetic
and authorize only this disposable World. No real account or production credential is present.

The fixture contains five identities, three chats, shared/reused ordinary and rich photos,
two emoji registrations sharing their assets, edits retaining old grants, pending bot updates,
answered and unanswered callbacks with original revisions, client changes, and isolated personas.
Two PNG images are generated by Pillow 12.3.0. The existing independently authored emoji inputs
are `tests/assets/custom-emoji/emoji-static.webp` and `emoji-thumbnail.webp`, with SHA-256 values
`7e1b283fb74b684cfaed135e5ce02ce6a0fc4824e4fb29c493f83fe05ccc0107` and
`6d97276da8fc4212d117000d1d0c0c83e86025004fd08257768d547e3527c034` respectively.
Photo and emoji admission still require their existing distinct image formats; shared storage
does not permit using WebP emoji file IDs as photos.

Retained output checksums:

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `world.sql` | `2079397fffaf7af5817b191012a2e4651b2c3143a48790faada3b14b508ce626` |
| `expected.json` | `8638fb11c4afbce68ecae79ddca2ae0d4ddb0fb1ebd52cc204c4fffa77f92a3f` |
| `identities.json` | `63955ca0d648fbcc55f2baafba3e49e66c6512fabdeffa25a35054d32bb0ec9f` |

For manual reproduction, provision this checkout's pinned offline environment, export only
`src/gramlab` from the base into a disposable directory, and select its `src` through
`PYTHONPATH`. Run `tests/fixtures/media_storage_v7/generate.py NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with this
checkout's `.venv/bin/python` through `tools/dev default --offline --command unshare --user
--map-root-user --net`. The generator refuses a different World source and an existing output
directory. It never runs during tests. New generation intentionally allocates new random World,
callback and file identities; compare the retained database with its retained outputs for literal
identity preservation. Do not replace the committed expectations with current implementation
outputs. Remove the disposable source export and regenerated output after review.

`test_media_storage_migration.py` checks complete outputs before/after reopen, all persisted rows
and exact bytes, real schema/index/FK compatibility, six interruption points including version
update, scheduled concurrent migration, corruption rejection, and grant/identity preservation.
Its initial baseline against schema 7 passed the full public-output comparisons and future-version
rejection; nine migration assertions failed as expected. The separately constructed empty v5
fixture in `test_media_world.py` is synthetic and removes all post-v5 tables explicitly.
